In 1999, Eastwood and Ezhov obtained a list of homogeneous
models by determining possible tangential vector ﬁelds. Inspired by Olver’s recurrence formulas,
we study the algebra of A(3) diﬀerential invariants of surfaces. We obtain necessary conditions

Introduction
In continuation with [18, 3, 2], we study the algebras of diﬀerential invariants of surfaces in
3-dimensional space, under the aﬃne A(3) — or special aﬃne SA(3) — transformation group.
To ﬁx the context, we work over C, and we study surfaces S2 ⊂C3 under A(3) whose Hessian
has (maximal) rank 2. We investigate ramiﬁcations of the Lie-Tresse theorem, following the
theory of Fels-Olver [11, 12].
Mainly, we explore what the powerful recurrence relations provide, ﬁrstly to determine the
structures of the concerned algebras of diﬀerential invariants, and secondly to determine all A(3)-
homogeneous nondegenerate surfaces S2 ⊂C3. The homogeneous classiﬁcation was terminated
in [1, 7, 9], without regard to algebras of diﬀerential invariants.
Interestingly, we really need to know the explicit expressions of certain key (relative or abso-
lute) diﬀerential invariants which create bifurcation branches.

Abstract: Consider a graphed holomorphic surface u = F(x, y) in C3 x,y,u under the action of the aﬃne transformation group A(3). In 1999, Eastwood and Ezhov obtained a list of homogeneous models by determining possible tangential vector ﬁelds. Inspired by Olver’s recurrence formulas, we study the algebra of A(3) diﬀerential invariants of surfaces. We obtain necessary conditions for homogeneity of algebraic nature. Solving these conditions, we organise homogeneous models in inequivalent branches.
